findings.summary: M18.10's evidence path will stall about 18 h behind a nightly that cannot qualify. db11774's fixed group `nightly` with cancel-in-progress false runs one nightly and keeps one pending run. Today's schedule (cron 02:17, created about 09:20Z on each of the last five days) starts before the tzap 0.1.2 bump is allowed (about 14:09Z), so it runs at 0.1.1. 41806720128 at 0.1.1 took 18 h 11 min and lost 30 shards, so this run cannot qualify either, and it holds the group until about 03:30Z on 2026-11-06. A workflow_dispatch sent after the bump to time the 30 shards would wait pending behind it, and GitHub cancels a pending run when a newer run of the group queues. The acceptance allows a dispatch run as the evidence, but nothing says the dispatch must be running rather than pending, or who may cancel a doomed 0.1.1 nightly. That decision is a run cancellation under the still-open cp42 F4 card.

findings.failure_scenario: The 0.1.1 nightly starts at about 09:20Z. The bump lands at 14:09Z, and its timing dispatch sits pending until 03:30Z the next day. Then that day's 09:20Z schedule queues during the dispatch, or replaces it if the dispatch is still pending. M18.10 slips a day or two per try, with M18.236 and M18.43 behind it. Or someone cancels the 0.1.1 run with no logged authority.

findings.summary: Two product rows landed through the staged test leg after it had refused one of them on a known-red seed. That is a re-roll of a failing gate, which the backlog's 'zero retries' forbids. Locally FC_SEED is '' unless CI is set (vitest.config.ts:65), so fast-check picks a fresh seed on every run. Seed 1397724349 refused M18.271's first land. M18.271 then landed anyway at 1093993 (committed 04:18:33Z), and M18.267 at 980429d (04:38:17Z). The property was unchanged in both trees, and only 712732b (05:21:41Z) fixed it. The defect was in the test, so no product harm came of it this time. But the same path lets a real counterexample, such as a geometry or undo invariant, be landed past by running the land again. Nothing records the refusing seed, and M18.274's progress entry does not say the row it blocked had already landed. M18.274 itself was the right response: a row for a land-blocking test defect, test-only, with two reviews, and check-checkpoint at 7/8. It should have taken the slot before M18.271's second land.
